messages:
Alice P.: quick sync — ACME (pilot customer) wants a tight onramp for a new add-on they call 'Performance Pack' (dedicated per-route throughput + burst credits + regional egress whitelist). They want commercials and a sign-off in ~2 weeks. Can we scope what we can actually promise and what needs addendum? :eyes:
Ben S.: they told us price is negotiable if SLA + burst guaranteed. main asks I heard: 200 rps per route sustained, 10k burst credits/month, regional egress control, SLA credits for tail latency. They want a 90-day pilot.
Diego M.: engineering note: 200 rps "guarantee" implies reserved/dedicated capacity or strict throttling + autoscale. We can hit it but requires a dedicated pool + autoscaler tuning + per-route isolation. Estimated infra work: ~2 weeks of eng (infra + QA) + config for canary. KV cache stickiness could reduce tail latencies but complicates multi-tenant routing.
Erin K.: finance: need a pricing structure that compensates reserved capacity. Proposal: base monthly reserved fee + per-1000-reqs overage + prepaid burst credits. Example: $5k/month reserved + $0.005 per extra request + $800 per 10k burst credits. We should model NPV for 90-day pilot.
Carla L.: legal: regional egress whitelist and data residency are doable but will need addendum (networking + audit logs). Cannot promise unconditional latency SLA across public cloud regions; must include carveouts (maintenance, force majeure, sustained DDoS, cross-region network variance). For pilot we can do a limited warranty and a defined rollback/backoff policy.
Frank R.: support: we'll need a runbook and playbook for failovers and capacity alerts. Also training for SEs and escalation paths. Recommend 'support readiness' be a launch gate.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging: perf-pack-v1 -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
Alice P.: thanks. I'm proposing concrete launch criteria so we can decide yes/no to ACME timeline. Draft launch criteria: 1) Perf tests show sustained 200 rps per route with 99.9% of requests < 300ms under customer-like workload; 2) Billing model approved by finance and pricing deck + example contract; 3) Legal sign-off on addendum covering egress/residency + SLA carveouts; 4) Support runbook + on-call training completed; 5) Telemetry + alerting (per-route cost, p95/p99 latency, quota burn) wired to console. Thoughts? :+1:
Diego M.: Criteria 1 is testable. We'll add a perf harness and a repeatable scenario. Small config example we'll add to README for customers:
```
route:
  name: acme-payment
  performance_pack_enabled: true
  reserved_capacity: 200
  burst_credits: 10000
```
We'll also add a feature flag: perf_pack.canary=true so we can roll back quickly.
Ben S.: ACME wants flexible commits. If we offer a 90-day pilot with a lower reserved fee and optional full commitment after pilot, they sign. We should draft a pilot commercial that includes specified ramp milestones.
Erin K.: pilot commercial sounds good. We need a [pilot-to-commit] conversion clause and a minimum conversion window documented. Also propose limited discount for pilot but require 30 days notice before termination to avoid churn.
Carla L.: legal agrees to a pilot addendum with limited liability and explicit termination triggers. We'll prepare a template; can't commit enterprise SLA without exec approval.
Frank R.: support will draft a short runbook template. Also ask for an observability dashboard sample to be included in onboarding.
Alice P.: action items: Diego -> perf harness + canary config (owner: Diego, ETA 10 business days). Erin -> price modeling + pilot commercial term (owner: Erin, ETA 3 business days). Carla -> draft pilot addendum + redlines (owner: Carla, ETA 5 business days). Ben -> negotiate pilot acceptance criteria with ACME and confirm timeline (owner: Ben, ETA 2 business days). Frank -> runbook skeleton + monitoring widgets (owner: Frank, ETA 7 business days). I'll own the final launch checklist and coordinate.
Diego M.: noted. I'll include metric names (redwood.performance.rps, redwood.latency.p99) and a load script for perf team.
Ben S.: ACME said they'd accept limited egress ZIP-level whitelisting if legal stamps it. Good sign.
Carla L.: will add residency/egress clauses and an initial security questionnaire item.
Alice P.: final check — does everyone agree we should not commit to cross-region hard latency SLA for pilot? keep it single-region guaranteed and multi-region best-effort.
Carla L.: agree. single-region warranty is fine for pilot.
Erin K.: agree, finance prefers single-region to limit risk.
Frank R.: agree. Support capacity is easier with single-region.
Alice P.: perfect. I'll send a short summary to ACME and schedule a 1:1 to walk through pilot terms. Thanks all :heart:
notes: Thread focuses on pricing/packaging-driven decision for a new Performance Pack add-on; short Slack-style messages with owners and launch criteria.
